‹#›Variables are very similar to algebra that we have learnt in Mathematics. Besides, they are like boxes for storing objects in our daily life. A name is labelled on each box for identifying the content. Variables can store various types of data, such as numbers or text. Different data types will be explained in detail later.

Input statements‹#›CPython asks users to input data by themselves through the input() function. The input obtained will be stored as a string in a variable. If we need to change its data type, we may use the int() or float() function.Printing instructions before receiving the users’ input allows them to know what they need to input. If we add a string into the input() function, the program prints a message before the keyboard cursor on the same line. For instance, “name = input("Please input your name: ")”.

Algorithms1.1An algorithm is a set of steps for solving a problem in the specified order. This process of comprehending an algorithm or a program is called “dry run”, which is a commonly used technique for deducing the purpose and output of an algorithm or a program.

Control Structures‹#›1.4In computer algorithms, there are three basic types of control structures, including sequence, selection and iteration. The sequence control structure allows the program to execute statements according to the order of writing. Selection and iteration control structures let the program decide which statements to execute according to specified conditions.
Selection‹#›ASelection control structure uses a Boolean expression as the condition for evaluation. The logical result will decide which statements the program should execute.
